display_name: The Entry into Israel Law, 5712-1952: the cross-references of section 12A1 and two more citations by address (with a control), and one waiting period, as typed values, with the defects kept as expected-red tests
domain_expert_review: none: no domain expert has read this against the source
scope: targeted row: records cross-references, citations by address and one waiting period from the Law, two sets of regulations and one schedule; it is not an encoding of the Law and asks no question from the seat

source.note: unofficial consolidation; every quotation from it is CONSOLIDATION-ONLY unless the row says it was read on a page image of the Knesset's Sefer HaChukim PDF
source.pdf_note: every PDF deposited is an extract of only the pages the row reads; SOURCES.json holds the whole file's sha256, size and page count as downloaded. SH 3441 p. 725 is deposited as a cropped image of the lines read, with no PDF page

expected_red.note: D1 (two assertions): section 12A1(a)(2)(b) cites section 32 of the Criminal Procedure Law, which is repealed (SH 1592 p. 350, section 41), where paragraph (1) of the same subsection names section 32 of the Ordinance. S2, S3 (one assertion each): regulation 21 cites section 13(a) and item 4(c) of the First Schedule of the Body Search Law cites section 12(1), where each number now names something else or nothing (SH 1804 pp. 502-503; SH 3441 p. 725). P1 against P3 (one assertion): regulation 21 gives a period of three days and section 13(d) as read by the 2026 temporary provision gives 24 hours for the class of persons in section 13(e). Each passes when the defect is removed. The enacting-formula citation "13(d)" in the 1985 expenses regulations is not a defect and is not in the count.

check.note: the five errors are the five expected failed assertions

run.method: one Sonnet encoder, no sub-agents, from a written brief; the page images were read by the encoder
